Question: default vs static method
Answer:
• Default methods are inherited by implementation classes to support backward compatibility, while static methods belong strictly to the interface and cannot be overridden
  • Key Differences
    • Instance vs. Class: Default methods require an object instance to run. Static methods are called directly using the interface name
    • Inheritance: Default methods are inherited by classes and can be overridden. Static methods are not inherited by implementation classes or subclasses
    • Multiple Inheritance Conflict: If a class implements two interfaces with the exact same default method, the class must override and resolve the conflict. This is not an issue for static methods because they are never inherited

Question: TDD, BDD, Pair Programming
Answer:
• TDD (Test-Driven Development): A developer-centric workflow where you write a failing automated test first, then write minimal production code to pass it, and finally clean the code.
  • BDD (Behavior-Driven Development): A collaborative workflow where business stakeholders and developers use plain human language (Given-When-Then) to define how a feature behaves before writing code.
  • Pair Programming: A teamwork practice where two developers share one screen, with one "Driver" typing the code and one "Navigator" reviewing it in real time.
  • I view TDD, BDD, and Pair Programming not just as coding practices, but as strategic engineering guardrails that align business intent with modular software design, drastically reducing long-term maintenance costs and alignment gaps.
